narrative:
The model has analyzed your academic journey and determined that there’s a **22% chance** you may not pass your final year. While this isn’t a certainty, it’s high enough that the school has decided you should take extra remedial courses to help you succeed. Think of it like a warning sign on a road—it’s not saying you *will* fail, but it’s telling you to slow down and take precautions.

The biggest reason behind this recommendation is your **number of past class failures**, which is currently at zero—this actually works *in your favor*. Most students who don’t need extra help have had no failures too, so this factor is helping your case. However, two other key aspects are raising concerns.

First, your **parents’ education level** is lower than average for students who pass without extra support. While many students succeed even when their parents haven’t gone to college, research shows that higher education levels at home often provide extra guidance and resources. This isn’t a guarantee of failure, but it’s a factor the model noticed could make success slightly harder.

Second, your **aspirations for higher education** are strong—this is a positive sign, as students who want to go further often work harder. However, the model also picked up on something else: your **school absences** are significantly higher than average. While most students miss only a few days, you’ve missed nine so far. Even small absences add up, and missing class time can make it harder to keep up, especially in a tough final year.

The good news? You’re not alone in this. The school is giving you a chance to get extra help now, before it’s too late. Focus on reducing absences, seek out any additional support your family or school can offer, and use these remedial courses as a way to strengthen your weak spots. With effort, you can still reach your goal of higher education—this is just a nudge to make sure you’re on the right path.
